title: Zeroed Counter Prefix
statement: Let $A$ be a counting-sort argument, let $j\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mu'$ be an integer-valued memory map. The first $j$ counter cells, starting at the counter region's initial address, contain zero: for every $t<j$, the memory value at address $A.cnt+t$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: μ' maps natural-number addresses to integers
every counter cell at offset t<j contains zero
